caitlynAuthorisation.about: The entity types @permission may name, read by the CaitlynPermissions lint rule. Every entity type is checked through the app's role grants (src/constants/roles/entities.ts); `grantTypes` lists the grants a role can hold on it, and @permission's `level` must be one of them. The permission names themselves come from permissions.json, which is generated.

agents.description: An agent; version access is checked on the agent's version access grant.

clients.description: An organisation-scoped grant ('own' or '*'), meaning where the role is held, never a record identifier.

conversations.description: A conversation. Checked through role grants like every other entity, so shared conversations need no second mechanism. Owner is a native grant type: the person or client that creates a conversation is given the owner grant on it, which includes every other level.

policy-sets.description: A policy. The entity type keeps the app's existing name, like the OAuth scope.

caitlynGlossary.about: The v3 vocabulary, read by the CaitlynBannedTerms lint rule. One concept has one name across the model: use the term listed here, and when a concept is not listed, add it in the same merge request as the model change. A change to this file needs a design owner's approval (CODEOWNERS). Source: the v3 API design guide, section 2, and the proposal's glossary.

banned.why: Settled product vocabulary; 'tenant' is the code's word.

banned.use: version (AgentVersion, addressed by draft, production or a version name)
banned.why: A version is the public name for an alias; 'alias' also means a workspace's extra hostnames. Covers agentAliasId, TSTALIASID and PRDALIASID.
Settled vocabulary. Not checked in documentation, where 'set' is an ordinary English verb.
'session' is a sign-in mode, never a chat.
'session' is a sign-in mode, never a chat.
A knowledge base item is a document. A file's name on the caller's machine (FileName, fileName) is not a knowledge base item.
A knowledge base item is a document. Files attached in chat (maxFiles) are not knowledge base items.
Never an address; the digest is a sha256 field.
Never an address; the digest is a sha256 field.
Implementation terms never appear on the public surface.
Version markers never appear on the public surface.

banned.use: send a message (the send custom method)
contentSafety on a version; the read-only GET /v3/guardrails list
status processing with an open stage string
status processing with an open stage string
status processing with an open stage string

recordedExceptions.why: OAuth scope names are shared with the MCP surface and held by issued credentials, so they are never renamed (design guide, section 2).
OAuth scope names are never renamed (design guide, section 2).
Permission names in @permission use the app's existing vocabulary (AUTH_SETTINGS), which the lint does not check.

terms.meaning: One Caitlyn deployment to an AWS account; can hold several organisations. Never in a public path or name; appears only as read-only support metadata on Workspace.
A client on an instance: one primary workspace and any number of child workspaces. Read-only in the public API (GET /v3/organisation).
A space bound to a subdomain, belonging to an organisation. The current one is implied by the hostname.
The assistant people chat with, configured through its versions.
One configuration of an agent, addressed by draft, production or a version name. The public name for what the code calls an alias.
A chat between a caller and an agent. The code calls it a session.
A collection of rules a policy review checks against. Never 'set' or 'policy set'.
One item in a knowledge base, stable across new uploads of new bytes.

Background work that continues after the request that started it.

A registered machine client (ApiClient). Replaces 'machine integration' and 'API integration'.
A workspace's address (hostname, additionalHostnames). Replaces 'domain' as a resource.

caitlynPermissions.generatedBy: scripts/smithyPermissionCatalogue.ts from AUTH_SETTINGS and the API scope catalogue. Do not edit by hand.

caitlynTelemetryAttributes.about: Stand-in for the OpenTelemetry Weaver attribute registry, which Gate 2 creates. The CaitlynTelemetryAttributes lint rule checks every @spanAttribute against this list; when the registry exists, this file is generated from it instead. Source: the design doc, 'Observability (OpenTelemetry)'.

caitlynVerbs.about: The approved verbs, read by the CaitlynOperationVerb and CaitlynPathForm lint rules. A verb not listed here fails the build until a design owner approves it and it is added in the same merge request (design guide, section 5).

eventNameExceptions.name: text.delta
eventNameExceptions.why: A fragment rather than a state change; 'delta' is the name every streaming AI API uses (Sam, 9 November 2026).

suppressions.reason: Identifier members such as uploadId and knowledgeBaseId would need @references. No SDK generator uses @references yet (agreed with the generator trial, 9 November 2026); revisit when references drive SDK helpers.

A read whose data is sensitive (personal data, an export, a transcript). It is audited like a
write: the `attempted` event is awaited before the data goes out, the request is refused with
503 when no audit event can be recorded, and the event is kept in the audit table. Writes are
always audited this way and do not carry the trait. Every other read publishes only its
outcome, and is served even when that event cannot be published.

The member may be named in the update's `clear` list, which returns it to its default.
Naming any other member in `clear` is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`.
The client namespace, lower camel case and plural, for example "conversations".
The method name, lower camel case, for example "send".

Where an operation appears in the SDKs' method-style clients, for example namespace
"documents", name "list". Python snake-cases the name. Needed only where the resource model
does not give the right name (PROTOCOL.md, section 10).

The stable problem `code` values an error shape carries. One error shape per HTTP status
(PROTOCOL.md, lint rule 1), so every code for that status is listed here. Codes are
UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, at most 63 characters, and never renamed once shipped.

Callers who opt into the SDK's `beta` namespace; may change.
Only callers with a debug permission.
Only when the setting that controls it is on (for example `deniedDocuments` on a version).
Who receives an event on a stream. Every member of an `@sseEvents` union declares exactly one.

The filters a List accepts: each key is an item member (dots for nested members, for example
"target.type") and each value lists the operators allowed on it. An undeclared field or
operator is refused with 400 `UNKNOWN_FILTER`.

The operation issues or revokes credentials, so no token may call it: its permission belongs to
no scope, and any token is refused with 403 `NOT_AVAILABLE_TO_CREDENTIALS`. A credential that
could mint credentials would escape its own revocation.
Why no audit event is needed.
The operation is not audited. Meant only for operations such as the health check.
The permission, for example "agents.update".

The record the grant check follows. Required on every operation that takes a record
identifier.
On a List: the entity type whose grants filter the list inside the database query.

The credential types allowed to call the operation. Absent means people only (a browser
session, or a token acting as one person). Machine clients and guest tokens must be listed.

`primary` on operations that only the organisation's primary workspace serves; elsewhere
they are refused with 403 `PRIMARY_WORKSPACE_REQUIRED`.

The permission an operation checks, in the app's existing permission vocabulary
(`AUTH_SETTINGS`). The OAuth scope is derived from it by the scope catalogue, never written by
hand. The generated wrapper checks, in order: caller type (403), primary workspace (403), the
permission (403), then the entity, version and document checks (404).

Authors write `@since("next")`. The release step replaces every "next" with the release number
when the model is published (smithy/scripts/stamp-since.sh), so a hand-typed number can never
name the wrong release. The SDK refuses to call an operation, or send a member, that is newer
than the server's `Caitlyn-Api-Version`.

Sends a message and streams the answer as server-sent events.

The stream ends with exactly one `message.completed` or `message.failed`. If the connection
drops, the SDK re-attaches with `ResumeConversationStream` and `Last-Event-ID`, so no event is
lost or repeated. Not retried automatically: a send that fails before the stream starts is
reported to the caller.

Members that are absent stay unchanged, nested objects are merged and lists are replaced whole.

and its new ETag.

Defines the ARN template. The provided string contains URI-template
style label placeholders that contain the name of one of the identifiers
defined in the `identifiers` property of the resource. These labels can
be substituted at runtime with the actual identifiers of the resource.
Every identifier name of the resource MUST have corresponding label of
the same name. Note that percent-encoding **is not** performed on these
placeholder values; they are to be replaced literally. For relative ARN
templates that have not set `absolute` to `true`, the template string
contains only the resource part of the ARN (for example,
`foo/{MyResourceId}`). Relative ARNs MUST NOT start with "/".

Set to true to indicate that the ARN template contains a fully-formed
ARN that does not need to be merged with the service. This type of ARN
MUST be used when the identifier of a resource is an ARN or is based on
the ARN identifier of a parent resource.

Set to true to specify that the ARN does not contain a region. If not
set, or if set to false, the resolved ARN will contain a placeholder
for the region. This can only be set to true if `absolute` is not set
or is false.

Set to true to specify that the ARN does not contain an account ID. If
not set, or if set to false, the resolved ARN will contain a placeholder
for the customer account ID. This can only be set to true if absolute
is not set or is false.

Defines which character is used to delimit sections of the resource

The `sdkId` property is a required string value that specifies the AWS
SDK service ID (e.g., "API Gateway"). This value is used for generating
client names in SDKs and for linking between services.

The `arnNamespace` property is a string value that defines the ARN service
namespace of the service (e.g., "apigateway"). This value is used in
ARNs assigned to resources in the service. If not set, this value
defaults to the lowercase name of the service shape.

The `cloudFormationName` property is a string value that specifies the
AWS CloudFormation service name (e.g., `ApiGateway`). When not set,
this value defaults to the name of the service shape. This value is
part of the CloudFormation resource type name that is automatically
assigned to resources in the service (e.g., `AWS::<NAME>::resourceName`).

The `cloudTrailEventSource` property is a string value that defines the
AWS customer-facing eventSource property contained in CloudTrail event
records emitted by the service. If not specified, this value defaults
to the `arnNamespace` plus `.amazonaws.com`.

The `docId` property is a string value that defines the identifier
used to implement linking between service and SDK documentation for
AWS services. If not specified, this value defaults to the `sdkId` in
lower case plus the service `version` property, separated by dashes.

The `endpointPrefix` property is a string value that identifies which
endpoint in a given region should be used to connect to the service.
For example, most services in the AWS standard partition have endpoints
which follow the format: `{endpointPrefix}.{region}.amazonaws.com`. A
service with the endpoint prefix example in the region us-west-2 might
have the endpoint example.us-west-2.amazonaws.com.

This value is not unique across services and is subject to change.
Therefore, it MUST NOT be used for client naming or for any other
purpose that requires a static, unique identifier. sdkId should be used
for those purposes. Additionally, this value can be used to attempt to
resolve endpoints.

The `cloudWatchNamespace` property is a string value that defines the
AWS customer-facing namespace of most metrics emitted by the service.

The signature version 4 service signing name to use in the credential
scope when signing requests. This value SHOULD match the `arnNamespace`
property of the `aws.api#service` trait if present and the `name`

[Signature Version 4](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html)
is the process to add authentication information to AWS requests sent by HTTP. For
security, most requests to AWS must be signed with an access key, which consists
of an access key ID and secret access key. These two keys are commonly referred to
as your security credentials.

Signature Version 4 Asymmetric (SigV4A), an extension of Signature Version 4 (SigV4), is the
process to add authentication information to AWS requests sent by HTTP. SigV4A is nearly
identical to SigV4, but also uses public-private keys and asymmetric cryptographic signatures
for every request. Most notably, SigV4A supports signatures for multi-region API requests.

breakingChanges.message: Removing the trait removes the ability for clients to do request or response checksums. The service MUST continue to support old clients by supporting the `httpChecksum` trait.

`requestAlgorithmMember` was removed, so newly generated clients will no longer be able to pick the request checksum algorithms The service MUST continue to support old clients by supporting `requestAlgorithmMember`.

`requestValidationModeMember` was removed, so newly generated clients will no longer validate response checksums. The service MUST continue to support old clients by supporting `requestValidationModeMember`.

Members of `responseAlgorithms` were removed, so newly generated clients will no longer validate response checksums for the removed algorithms. The service MUST continue to support old clients by supporting removed compression algorithms.
